steps: Heat a little oil in a pan and fry the curry paste or powder for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the sweet potato cubes, stir to coat, and cook for 3-4 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk, add the chickpeas, cover and simmer for 15-18 minutes until the sweet potato is tender.
Stir through the spinach and cook for 2 minutes until wilted; season to taste.
Serve hot over the cooked basmati rice, divided across 5 portions.
Cut the chicken breast into bite-sized pieces and season lightly with salt.
Sear the chicken in a hot pan with a little oil for 4-5 minutes until browned and cooked through, then set aside.
Warm the tikka masala sauce in the same pan over medium heat for 3-4 minutes.
Return the chicken to the sauce and simmer for 5 minutes until piping hot and well coated.
Scatter with chopped coriander and serve over the basmati rice.
Lightly mash the cooked rice with the back of a spoon to break up any lumps.
Stir in the yogurt and a splash of water until creamy, then season with salt.
Heat the oil in a small pan and add the mustard seeds; once they start to pop, add the curry leaves and grated ginger and fry for 30 seconds.
Pour the sizzling tempering over the yogurt rice and mix through.
Top with pomegranate seeds or halved grapes and serve at room temperature or chilled.
Finely chop the onion and cook it low and slow in a splash of oil for 15-20 minutes, stirring often, until soft and deep golden.
Stir in the berbere or curry spice blend and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chopped tomato and the red lentils, cover with water or stock, and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils break down into a thick stew.
Season with salt, then spoon the misir wat over the injera.
Serve with a halved hard-boiled egg and the cooked cabbage and carrot side.
Heat the oil in a pot and fry the chopped onion for 3-4 minutes until soft.
Add the chopped tomato and bell pepper and cook for 5 minutes until the tomato breaks down.
Stir in the boiled maize and cooked beans, add a splash of water, cover and simmer for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Season with salt and pepper and serve hot.
For the stew, brown the beef in a little oil, then add chopped onion and tomato and cook until softened; cover with water and simmer for 45-60 minutes until tender.
For the ugali, bring water to the boil in a heavy pan, then sprinkle in the maize meal in small amounts while stirring constantly to stop lumps forming.
Keep stirring and pressing with a wooden spoon as the mixture thickens into a stiff, smooth dough, about 8-10 minutes.
Meanwhile, wilt the managu, or spinach/collard greens, in a splash of water or oil for 3-4 minutes.
Turn the ugali out onto a plate and serve with the beef stew and greens alongside.
Finely chop the onion, carrot and celery.
Brown the mince in a little oil over high heat, season with salt, then set aside.
In the same pan, sauté the chopped onion, carrot and celery over a lower heat until softened but not browned.
Stir in the tomato sauce, return the browned mince to the pan, cover and simmer for 30 minutes.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.
Serve over freshly cooked spaghetti with grated parmesan.
Cook the gluten-free pasta according to the pack instructions, then drain.
Meanwhile, warm the marinara sauce in a pan over medium heat.
Stir in the cooked lentils and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until heated through and slightly thickened.
Stir in the nutritional yeast and season to taste.
Toss with the cooked pasta and finish with torn basil.
Preheat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Cook the ziti in salted boiling water until just al dente, then drain.
If using, brown the turkey mince in a pan, then stir in the marinara sauce and simmer for 5 minutes.
Mix the cooked ziti through the sauce, then fold in the ricotta.
Transfer to a baking dish, top with the mozzarella, and cover with foil.
Bake for 20 minutes covered, then uncover and bake for a further 10 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbling.
Cook the fusilli in salted boiling water until al dente, then drain and rinse under cold water.
Halve the cherry tomatoes and dice the cucumber.
Slice the grilled chicken into strips.
Toss the pasta with the chicken, tomatoes, cucumber and olive oil in a large bowl.
Scatter with grated parmesan and torn basil, and season to taste before serving.
Heat a little oil in a large pot and sauté the chopped carrot and celery for 4-5 minutes until starting to soften.
Add the chopped courgette and tomato and cook for a further 3-4 minutes.
Pour in the vegetable stock, bring to a simmer, and cook for 15 minutes.
Add the cannellini beans and small pasta, and simmer for a further 10 minutes until the pasta is tender.
Season to taste, ladle into bowls, and serve with grated parmesan and a slice of bread.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot and sauté the chopped onion, carrot and celery for 5 minutes until softened.
Stir in the chopped tomato and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the lentils and vegetable stock, bring to the boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 20 minutes until the lentils are tender.
Blend part of the soup with a stick blender for a thicker texture, if you like, then season to taste.
Serve hot with the wholegrain bread.
Peel and cube the butternut squash.
Heat a little oil in a pot, add the grated ginger and cumin, and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the squash and vegetable stock, bring to the boil, then simmer for 15-18 minutes until the squash is tender.
Stir in the drained chickpeas and coconut milk, then blend until smooth with a stick blender.
Season to taste and serve with the cooked rice on the side.
Heat a little oil in a pot and sauté the chopped onion, carrot and celery for 5 minutes until softened.
Pour in the chicken stock and bring to the boil.
Add the rice and simmer for 12-15 minutes until tender.
Stir in the shredded roast chicken and heat through for 2-3 minutes.
Season to taste, stir through the chopped parsley, and serve.
